explanation_en: The adjective 'decidido' combined with the preposition 'a' and an infinitive means 'determined to' do something. It expresses a strong, firm resolve and is much more powerful than simply saying 'querer' or 'intentar'. It is a common collocation in political, sports, and motivational contexts.

examples.en_text: The neighbors are determined to fight for the neighborhood park.
examples.target_text: Los vecinos están decididos a luchar por el parque del barrio.

examples.en_text: Despite the difficulties, she showed she was determined to fight for her career.
examples.target_text: A pesar de las dificultades, ella se mostró decidida a luchar por su carrera.

examples.en_text: The team's players entered the field determined to fight for the victory.
examples.target_text: Las jugadoras del equipo entraron al campo decididas a luchar por la victoria.

examples.en_text: The young entrepreneur is determined to fight to make his business successful.
examples.target_text: El joven emprendedor está decidido a luchar para que su negocio tenga éxito.

examples.en_text: We are determined to fight against climate change in our community.
examples.target_text: Estamos decididos a luchar contra el cambio climático en nuestra comunidad.

examples.en_text: The workers remained determined to fight for their rights during the strike.
examples.target_text: Los trabajadores se mantuvieron decididos a luchar por sus derechos durante la huelga.

explanation_en: 'Dejar al descubierto' literally means to leave uncovered, but it is frequently used metaphorically to mean 'to expose,' 'to reveal,' or 'to lay bare' secrets, flaws, or physical objects. It is a sophisticated alternative to 'revelar' or 'mostrar'. Ensure you use the preposition 'al' (contraction of 'a' + 'el') before 'descubierto'.

examples.en_text: The strong wind took off the tarp and left the new car uncovered.
examples.target_text: El fuerte viento quitó la lona y dejó al descubierto el coche nuevo.

examples.en_text: The press's latest investigation exposes the corruption in the company.
examples.target_text: La última investigación de la prensa deja al descubierto la corrupción en la empresa.

examples.en_text: His nervous reaction reveals that he doesn't have much experience in this job.
examples.target_text: Su reacción nerviosa deja al descubierto que no tiene mucha experiencia en este trabajo.

examples.en_text: When the tide goes down, the sea leaves some beautiful rocks exposed.
examples.target_text: Cuando baja la marea, el mar deja al descubierto unas rocas preciosas.

examples.en_text: The system failure exposed the users' private data.
examples.target_text: El fallo del sistema dejó al descubierto los datos privados de los usuarios.

examples.en_text: That short shirt leaves the tattoo on his back exposed.
examples.target_text: Esa camiseta tan corta deja al descubierto el tatuaje que tiene en la espalda.

explanation_en: This adverbial locution is a very natural synonym for 'completamente' or 'totalmente'. It is placed after the verb it modifies to emphasize the absolute nature of an action. It is widely used across all registers, from casual conversation to formal writing.

examples.en_text: I completely forgot that we had a meeting today.
examples.target_text: Se me olvidó por completo que hoy teníamos una reunión.

examples.en_text: He decided to completely change his life and moved to the countryside.
examples.target_text: Decidió cambiar de vida por completo y se mudó al campo.

examples.en_text: You have to erase the hard drive to completely clean the computer.
examples.target_text: Tienes que borrar el disco duro para limpiar el ordenador por completo.

examples.en_text: After the storm, the sky cleared up completely.
examples.target_text: Después de la tormenta, el cielo se despejó por completo.

examples.en_text: I completely trust your decision, I know you will do the right thing.
examples.target_text: Confío por completo en tu decisión, sé que harás lo correcto.

examples.en_text: They completely renovated the kitchen and now it looks much bigger.
examples.target_text: Reformaron la cocina por completo y ahora parece mucho más grande.

explanation_en: The adjective 'arraigado' comes from 'raíz' (root) and describes customs, beliefs, or practices that are firmly established and difficult to change. It is almost always paired with verbs like 'estar' or 'quedar'. It is a high-level vocabulary choice that adds a native touch when discussing traditions or systemic issues.

examples.en_text: This custom is deeply rooted in our region.
examples.target_text: Esta costumbre está muy arraigada en nuestra región.

examples.en_text: It is difficult to change these prejudices because they are deeply rooted in society.
examples.target_text: Es difícil cambiar estos prejuicios porque están muy arraigados en la sociedad.

examples.en_text: The habit of taking a siesta is deeply rooted in many towns in Spain.
examples.target_text: El hábito de dormir la siesta está muy arraigado en muchos pueblos de España.

examples.en_text: He has a fear of failure that is deeply rooted since childhood.
examples.target_text: Tiene un miedo al fracaso muy arraigado desde la infancia.

examples.en_text: Some superstitions are still deeply rooted among older people.
examples.target_text: Algunas supersticiones todavía están muy arraigadas entre la gente mayor.

examples.en_text: Respect for nature is a value deeply rooted in this community.
examples.target_text: El respeto por la naturaleza es un valor muy arraigado en esta comunidad.

explanation_en: The adjective 'reacio' means reluctant, hesitant, or opposed to something, and it is typically followed by the preposition 'a'. The collocation 'reacio al riesgo' is the standard Spanish translation for 'risk-averse'. It is very common in professional, financial, and scientific discussions.

examples.en_text: Many traditional investors are risk-averse and prefer to buy government bonds.
examples.target_text: Muchos inversores tradicionales son reacios al riesgo y prefieren comprar bonos del Estado.

examples.en_text: She is very risk-averse, so she decided to keep her stable job instead of starting a business.
examples.target_text: Ella es muy reacia al riesgo, por lo que decidió mantener su trabajo estable en lugar de emprender.

examples.en_text: Politicians tend to be risk-averse when elections are approaching.
examples.target_text: Los políticos suelen ser reacios al riesgo cuando se acercan las elecciones.

examples.en_text: My sisters are quite risk-averse and don't want to try adventure sports.
examples.target_text: Mis hermanas son bastante reacias al riesgo y no quieren probar los deportes de aventura.

examples.en_text: Our boss is a bit risk-averse, so it's hard to propose innovative ideas.
examples.target_text: Nuestro jefe es un poco reacio al riesgo, así que es difícil proponer ideas innovadoras.

examples.en_text: In times of crisis, consumers become more risk-averse with their purchases.
examples.target_text: En tiempos de crisis, los consumidores se vuelven más reacios al riesgo con sus compras.

explanation_en: This transition phrase is used to introduce the final, most fundamental level of a situation, or the ultimate decider/consequence. It is equivalent to 'ultimadamente' but sounds much more elegant and natural in written and spoken Spanish. It is highly useful for structuring arguments or lists in essays and presentations.

examples.en_text: Ultimately, the decision to accept the job is yours and no one else's.
examples.target_text: En última instancia, la decisión de aceptar el trabajo es tuya y de nadie más.

examples.en_text: The director is, ultimately, responsible for the success of the project.
examples.target_text: El director es, en última instancia, el responsable del éxito del proyecto.

examples.en_text: We try to help our son, but ultimately he has to learn from his own mistakes.
examples.target_text: Intentamos ayudar a nuestro hijo, pero en última instancia él tiene que aprender de sus propios errores.

examples.en_text: Although we analyzed many options, in the end we decided to buy the used car.
examples.target_text: Aunque analizamos muchas opciones, en última instancia decidimos comprar el coche usado.

examples.en_text: Doctors can give you advice, but ultimately it is up to you to take care of your health.
examples.target_text: Los médicos pueden darte consejos, pero en última instancia depende de ti cuidar tu salud.

examples.en_text: It is the citizens who, ultimately, choose the future of the country.
examples.target_text: Son los ciudadanos quienes, en última instancia, eligen el futuro del país.

explanation_en: This idiomatic phrase translates literally to 'the person on foot' but means 'the average citizen' or 'the man on the street'. It is widely used in journalism, politics, and everyday speech to contrast the general public with elites or corporations. It is a highly natural way to refer to ordinary people without sounding overly academic.

examples.en_text: The rise in electricity prices affects the average person above all.
examples.target_text: La subida de los precios de la luz afecta sobre todo a la persona de a pie.

examples.en_text: Politicians should speak more simply so that the man on the street can understand them.
examples.target_text: Los políticos deberían hablar de forma más sencilla para que la persona de a pie los entienda.

examples.en_text: How is artificial intelligence going to change the daily life of the average person?
examples.target_text: ¿Cómo va a cambiar la inteligencia artificial la vida diaria de la persona de a pie?

examples.en_text: Laws are sometimes so complicated that an ordinary person cannot understand them without help.
examples.target_text: Las leyes a veces son tan complicadas que una persona de a pie no puede comprenderlas sin ayuda.

examples.en_text: This type of abstract art is usually difficult for the average person to appreciate.
examples.target_text: Este tipo de arte abstracto suele ser difícil de apreciar para la persona de a pie.

examples.en_text: The new economic measures do not benefit average people, but rather large corporations.
examples.target_text: Las nuevas medidas económicas no benefician a las personas de a pie, sino a las grandes empresas.

explanation_en: This is a very common fixed adverbial phrase used to express absolute certainty. It is highly versatile and can be used at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence. It serves as a more elegant and idiomatic alternative to 'sin duda' or 'indudablemente'.

examples.en_text: Without a doubt, this has been the best trip of my life.
examples.target_text: Sin lugar a dudas, este ha sido el mejor viaje de mi vida.

examples.en_text: She is, without a doubt, the most qualified person for the job.
examples.target_text: Ella es, sin lugar a dudas, la persona más calificada para el puesto.

examples.en_text: The use of technology is going to change, undoubtedly, our way of working.
examples.target_text: El uso de la tecnología va a cambiar, sin lugar a dudas, nuestra forma de trabajar.

examples.en_text: Without a doubt, the food at this restaurant is excellent.
examples.target_text: Sin lugar a dudas, la comida de este restaurante es excelente.

examples.en_text: Making that decision was, without a doubt, a big mistake.
examples.target_text: Tomar esa decisión fue, sin lugar a dudas, un gran error.

examples.en_text: Autumn is, without a doubt, my favorite season of the year.
examples.target_text: El otoño es, sin lugar a dudas, mi estación del año favorita.

explanation_en: This is a sophisticated, high-register conjunction (B2/C1 level) that can mean 'since', 'given that', or 'as soon as' depending on the context. It is frequently used in formal journalism, legal documents, and academic discussions to establish a conditional or causal relationship. Learners should note that it is often followed by the subjunctive when referring to future, unfulfilled actions.

examples.en_text: Given that we do not have enough budget, we must reduce advertising expenses.
examples.target_text: Toda vez que no tenemos suficiente presupuesto, debemos reducir los gastos de publicidad.

examples.en_text: The project was canceled, since it did not comply with safety regulations.
examples.target_text: El proyecto fue cancelado, toda vez que no cumplía con las normas de seguridad.

examples.en_text: As soon as we receive your confirmation by email, we will send you the platform access details.
examples.target_text: Toda vez que recibamos tu confirmación por correo, te enviaremos los accesos a la plataforma.

examples.en_text: We cannot travel this weekend, given that I have to work on Saturday.
examples.target_text: No podemos viajar este fin de semana, toda vez que tengo que trabajar el sábado.

examples.en_text: Once you finish your studies, you will be able to apply for a position at our company.
examples.target_text: Toda vez que termines tus estudios, podrás postularte para un puesto en nuestra empresa.

examples.en_text: We decided to buy the used car, since the price was very convenient and it was in good condition.
examples.target_text: Decidimos comprar el coche usado, toda vez que el precio era muy conveniente y estaba en buen estado.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase is extremely common in news, business, and political registers. It translates to 'facing', 'with a view to', or 'in preparation for' a future event or challenge. It is a highly natural way to link current actions to future goals or scenarios.

examples.en_text: We have to improve our marketing strategy with a view to next year.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que mejorar nuestra estrategia de marketing de cara al próximo año.

examples.en_text: The students are reviewing the most difficult topics in preparation for the final exam.
examples.target_text: Los estudiantes están repasando los temas más difíciles de cara al examen final.

examples.en_text: We want to paint the house and fix up the garden in preparation for the summer.
examples.target_text: Queremos pintar la casa y arreglar el jardín de cara al verano.

examples.en_text: The government is proposing new measures with a view to the upcoming elections.
examples.target_text: El gobierno está proponiendo nuevas medidas de cara a las próximas elecciones.

examples.en_text: The team is training very hard in preparation for Sunday's match.
examples.target_text: El equipo está entrenando muy duro de cara al partido del domingo.

examples.en_text: It is important to learn languages with a view to your professional future.
examples.target_text: Es importante aprender idiomas de cara a tu futuro profesional.

explanation_en: This is the standard idiomatic translation for 'brain drain', referring to the emigration of highly trained or intelligent people from a particular country. It is a fixed collocation widely used in sociological, economic, and political journalism. It is essential vocabulary for discussing migration and economic development at an advanced level.

examples.en_text: The government is looking for measures to stop the brain drain in the technology sector.
examples.target_text: El gobierno está buscando medidas para frenar la fuga de cerebros en el sector tecnológico.

examples.en_text: Many young scientists are going abroad, which represents a serious brain drain for the country.
examples.target_text: Muchos jóvenes científicos se van al extranjero, lo que representa una grave fuga de cerebros para el país.

examples.en_text: If we don't improve professionals' salaries, the brain drain will continue to increase.
examples.target_text: Si no mejoramos los salarios de los profesionales, la fuga de cerebros continuará aumentando.

examples.en_text: The lack of opportunities in small provinces causes a constant brain drain toward the capital.
examples.target_text: La falta de oportunidades en las provincias pequeñas provoca una constante fuga de cerebros hacia la capital.

examples.en_text: To avoid brain drain, our company offers scholarships and professional development plans.
examples.target_text: Para evitar la fuga de cerebros, nuestra empresa ofrece becas y planes de desarrollo profesional.

examples.en_text: Brain drain is a serious problem that affects the economic development of Latin America.
examples.target_text: La fuga de cerebros es un problema grave que afecta al desarrollo económico de América Latina.

explanation_en: The phrase 'dar de alta' (or 'dar el alta' in some administrative contexts) means to officially register, activate, or onboard someone in a system, payroll, or social security. In medical contexts, it means to discharge a patient from the hospital. Its antonym is 'dar de baja' (to deregister or cancel a service/contract).

examples.en_text: Yesterday they finally onboarded me at the company and I already have my work email.
examples.target_text: Ayer por fin me dieron el alta en la empresa y ya tengo mi correo de trabajo.

examples.en_text: I called the electricity company and they told me they activated the service today.
examples.target_text: Llamé a la compañía de luz y me dijeron que hoy dieron el alta al servicio.

examples.en_text: The agent confirmed to me that they have already approved my registration as self-employed.
examples.target_text: El gestor me confirmó que ya le dieron el alta a mi solicitud de autónomo.

examples.en_text: As soon as they register me on the platform, I will be able to download the materials.
examples.target_text: En cuanto me den el alta en la plataforma, podré descargar los materiales.

examples.en_text: I went to the gym this morning and they registered me in the system immediately.
examples.target_text: Fui al gimnasio esta mañana y me dieron el alta en el sistema de inmediato.

examples.en_text: After sending the documents, they officially registered us as members of the club.
examples.target_text: Después de enviar los documentos, nos dieron el alta como socios del club.
